extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders in DOL FLSA overtime rulemaking (employers, employee representatives, labor lawyers, state AGs, policy analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and decision rationale for selecting and implementing the salary-level test that pairs with the standard duties test to define the bona fide executive, administrative, and professional (EAP) exemption under the FLSA. Covers data sources, percentile choice, geographic scope, and balancing employee protection with employer reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for shift to a one-test system
rubrics_metrics.description: When updating the salary level, the Department should account for the move from a two-test (long and short duties tests) to a one-test (standard duties) system because that shift decreased examination of nonexempt work and altered who is protected by the salary test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology should recognize that a single-test system cannot fully replicate the protections of the two-test system; therefore the salary level selected can and should be adjusted (in conjunction with the duties test) to better identify bona fide EAP employees and restore some protections historically provided by the long duties test. Antipattern: ignoring the one-test shift and leaving the entire burden of the change on employees who historically performed substantial nonexempt work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore the salary level's screening function
rubrics_metrics.description: The salary level should perform a screening function to help exclude from exemption lower-paid employees who perform substantial amounts of nonexempt work—i.e., restore the historic role of the salary test as a screening mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoring screening does not require returning fully to the long test or making salary determinative for all employees; instead it means choosing a salary level that excludes some employees who historically were nonexempt. Antipattern: setting a salary so low it fails to screen employees performing significant nonexempt work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a percentile-based salary level between long and short tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a salary level using an earnings-percentile approach located between the long test (historically ~25th percentile in low-wage areas) and the short test (around the midpoint) to calibrate exemption scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department used ventiles (30th, 35th, 40th, 45th, 50th percentiles) between the long and short test levels and selected the second-to-lowest ventile (35th) to balance protections and reliance interests. Example tradeoffs: 30th would insufficiently address one-test shift; 40th (2016 methodology) would make salary determinative for a larger share of workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set salary level at the 35th percentile in lowest-wage Census Region
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule sets the standard salary level equal to the 35th percentile of full-time salaried worker earnings in the lowest-wage Census Region (the South), producing $1,128 per week using 2023 data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific percentile was selected to distribute the impact of the move to a one-test system (approximately 40% of workers between long and short tests would be salary-determinative). It is presented as consistent with the Department's authority to define and delimit the EAP exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data from the lowest-wage Census Region (South) rather than nationwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the salary level using a lower-salary regional data set (the lowest-wage Census Region) to accommodate businesses and workers in areas where salaries are generally lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: BLS routinely compiles this data; it promotes transparency and regulatory simplification and accounts for regional/industry differences. Antipatterns: using nationwide data (would not account for low-wage areas) or narrowing further to very small regional/state subsets (would skew results and give undue weight to very low-wage areas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CPS MORG full-time nonhourly worker earnings as proxy for salaried earnings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relies on Current Population Survey (CPS) Merged Outgoing Rotation Group (MORG) data for nonhourly full-time workers as the best available proxy for salaried worker earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects excluding nonexempt workers from the data set or otherwise limiting to only exempt employees because that would require uncertain assumptions about which employees are exempt. Antipattern: restricting dataset to exempt workers or to a particular industry without robust statistical basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on up-to-date data when setting the salary level
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recent calendar-year earnings data (the final rule uses 2023 data) to calculate the percentile-based salary level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency practice: the NPRM provided estimates based on then-current data to inform comments; final determinations should use the most recent available BLS data. Antipattern: relying on outdated data or only inflation-adjusting decades-old nominal figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance employee protection with employer reliance interests
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting a salary level, weigh the need to restore overtime protection for employees who perform substantial nonexempt work against employers' reliance interests developed under prior lower salary levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing a level between long and short tests distributes the impact of the one-test shift across employees and employers. A substantially higher level could disrupt employer reliance; a substantially lower level would place the burden entirely on employees historically entitled to overtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the salary level does not supplant the duties test
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid setting the salary level so high that it becomes determinative of exemption status for too many employees and effectively supplants the duties test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen methodology should preserve the role of the duties test in determining exemption; comparisons (e.g., percent of between-long-and-short workers made salary-determinative) are used to assess this risk. Antipattern: selecting a percentile that would make salary the determinative test for the majority of affected employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using simple inflation-updating of historical levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical practice avoided relying on inflation indicators to update long test levels; updating by inflation alone (e.g., adjusting a 1975 nominal figure by inflation) would not faithfully replicate historical methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: applying a pure inflation-adjustment to an old long test figure (Oxford Economics suggestion) because it would produce a salary below the historic 10th percentile in low-wage areas and conflict with historical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not narrow the data set to very low-wage states/industries/entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject requests to restrict the data set to ten lowest-wage states, East South Central division, or to particular low-wage entities within industries because such restriction would inappropriately weight the lowest-earning areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data set purpose is not simply to produce the lowest possible salary level but to account for low-wage areas while being appropriate nationwide. Antipattern: compounding restrictions (low-wage entities within low-wage industries within rural South) which would skew the salary level downward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and justify percentile choice with quantitative tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative rationale for selecting a specific percentile (e.g., how many workers between long and short tests would be salary-determinative under alternatives: 30th -> 18%; 35th -> 40%; 40th -> 55%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule should show the distributional impacts of alternatives (number of affected workers, comparison to historical norms) so stakeholders can evaluate tradeoffs. Antipattern: asserting a percentile choice without showing distributional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor transparent, easily understood methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Select methods that are transparent, easily understood, and based on routinely compiled public data (e.g., BLS/CPS) to promote clarity and facilitate meaningful public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices that promote transparency include publishing the data year used, explaining why the data set was chosen, and providing projected figures in the NPRM so commenters can comment on likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and rely upon NPRM estimates to facilitate comment
rubrics_metrics.description: In the NPRM, include projected salary-level figures produced by the proposed methodology (even if based on preliminary data) to give stakeholders a concrete basis for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing estimates promotes rulemaking transparency and informed commenter feedback; critics who seized on projected figures do not thereby show prejudicial lack of meaningful opportunity to comment.
